questions.prompt: The Banach fixed-point theorem guarantees convergence of x <- f(x) when
options: f is continuous and maps a closed interval into itself, so a fixed point exists
the space is complete and |f(x)-f(y)| < |x-y| for all x != y, with f mapping it into itself
the space is complete, f maps it into itself, and f shrinks distances by a constant L < 1
f is differentiable everywhere with |f'(x)| <= 1, so the iterates move less each step
questions.explanation: A constant strictly below 1 is essential; x+1/x shrinks every pair yet has no fixed point.

questions.prompt: f(x)=cos x on [0,1] has contraction constant L=sin 1=0.8415. With |x1-x0|=0.3776, what is the a-priori error bound after n=10 steps? (3 decimals)
Value iteration with gamma=0.5 starts with sup-norm error 8. After how many sweeps is the guaranteed error at most 0.01? (integer)
Project y=(2,0) onto span{(1,1)}. What is the first coordinate of the projection?
The set {(x,y,z): x^2+y^2-z^2=0} is NOT a manifold at the origin because
options: the set is unbounded, so no finite atlas of charts can cover all of it
the Jacobian of the constraint vanishes there, so the regular-value test fails
the constraint has degree two, and only linear constraints define manifolds
the set contains the origin, and a manifold cannot contain the zero vector of the space
questions.explanation: Dg=2(x,y,-z)=0 at the origin; the cone has an apex.

questions.skillLabel: Dimension of a regular level set
questions.prompt: What is the dimension of the set {x in R^5 : g(x)=0} when g maps R^5 to R^2 and the Jacobian has rank 2 everywhere on the set?

Choose a theorem you want to rely on (for example convergence of a fixed-point solver). Write its hypotheses, explain how you would test each on your problem, and give a counterexample showing one of them cannot be dropped.
rubric: Lists the hypotheses explicitly and separately from the conclusion.
Gives a concrete numerical or analytic test for each hypothesis.
Provides a valid counterexample for a dropped hypothesis, such as x+1/x for L<1.
